newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervy Brussels bourse eyes U.S. data, German repo.
newsitem.headline: Nervy Brussels bourse eyes U.S. data, German repo.

text.p: A nervous Brussels bourse focused firmly on Monday on a tide of U.S. figures due later this week and possible Bundesbank action on the repo rate, but traders reported underlying support as bargain hunters appeared.
"The market will remain nervous in coming days. There is buying support. The institutions are buying, but cautiously," one trader said.

"People are waiting to see what the Bundesbank does on Tuesday, and what the U.S. data shows," she added. U.S. July retail sales and producer prices are due on Wednesday, with consumer prices and industrial production on Thursday.
Traders noted that players were focusing on individual stocks -- with some proving highly volatile and others rising steadily.
Banks proved a particular favourite on Monday, with Generale Bank and Kredietbank up 2.45 and 1.36 percent respectively.
Traders said the rise -- against a declining market -- was a reaction to the selling that hit the stocks late last week.
Chemical and drugs firm UCB epitomised the waves of buying and selling that swept the market. The share moved between 126,000 and 122,500 francs.
UCB ended the day down 3.39 percent at 122,650 francs.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert also experienced volatility, moving between 24,900 and 24,000 francs but ending right in the middle at 24,450 -- down 550 francs from Friday.
Hamburger chain Quick likewise continued to suffer from waves of popularity and unpopularity, swinging between 2,095 and 2,000 francs to end unchanged at 2,075.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares closed 0.45 percent lower at 2,420.57, having opened 1.6 percent down. A total of some four billion francs of shares changed hands.
